## How it works

- [statement] Tag selection does not itself bound replication lag. The server-selection specification applies maxStalenessSeconds before tag matching; its default imposes no maximum staleness. A strict analytics target can become ineligible when a configured staleness bound is exceeded. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes
- [statement] Historical issue SERVER-9984 describes mongos connection churn when clients alternated read-preference tags in MongoDB 2.4.4. The issue was closed as a duplicate with no fix version listed; it is historical operational evidence, not proof that current releases have this behavior. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-9984 · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes
- [statement] Appending an empty tag-set fallback weakens strict workload isolation: an empty tag set matches any otherwise eligible server, so secondary mode can fall back from analytics members to operational secondaries when the earlier tag set has no match. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/replica-set-tags.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For strict analytics-only read placement, use secondary mode with the ANALYTICS member tag and accept a selection failure when no matching secondary is eligible; allowing primary fallback defeats that isolation boundary. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/replica-set-tags.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md, https://pmclain.com/mongodb/2022/09/28/fun-with-mongodb-atlas-analytics-nodes.html
- [statement] An empty fallback tag set trades isolation for availability: Atlas documents that it permits any available secondary if no analytics member matches. Exclusive analytics targeting can instead fail during initial sync, disk scale-down or NVMe tier changes. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/replica-set-tags.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md
- [statement] secondaryPreferred is an isolation antipattern when analytics reads must never reach the primary: if no eligible tagged secondary exists, selection can choose the primary. A firsthand 2022 Atlas incident reports primary degradation from this fallback and recovery after switching the analytics client to secondary. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://pmclain.com/mongodb/2022/09/28/fun-with-mongodb-atlas-analytics-nodes.html
- [statement] A hidden secondary cannot serve reads through mongos. MongoDB warns that directly reading hidden shard members can produce inconsistent data or loss, and recommends tag-based read preferences for sharded workload isolation instead. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-hidden-member.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For a sharded client, read-preference mode, tags, and maximum staleness do not choose the mongos router; the driver passes these options to mongos. Workload-specific member selection therefore belongs behind the router rather than in direct shard connections. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-hidden-member.md, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Routing expensive reporting, ETL, or connector discovery reads to dedicated analytics secondaries separates their query execution from operational reads and writes; both MongoDB Atlas guidance and OVHcloud documentation describe this pattern, and Airbyte recommends it for discovery workloads. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/replica-set-tags.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/blob/master/docs/integrations/sources/mongodb-v2/mongodb-v2-troubleshooting.md, https://docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/public-cloud/databases/mongodb-analytics
- [statement] Airbyte documents a concrete pressure source: schema-enforced discovery runs concurrent aggregation pipelines across collections and can exhaust CPU and memory. Its proposed analytics-node alternative moves that work but does not reduce the discovery workload itself. (low confidence) — https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/blob/master/docs/integrations/sources/mongodb-v2/mongodb-v2-troubleshooting.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes
- [statement] Isolation should work in both directions: Atlas documents workloadType:OPERATIONAL for ordinary secondary readers so they exclude analytics nodes, complementing the separate analytics-only client. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/replica-set-tags.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://pmclain.com/mongodb/2022/09/28/fun-with-mongodb-atlas-analytics-nodes.html
- [statement] Do not treat a particular Atlas host name as a permanent analytics endpoint. Atlas warns that the same host name may refer to a different node type after a topology change. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-config/multi-cloud-distribution.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes
- [statement] Dedicated secondary routing does not guarantee fresh data: secondaries replicate asynchronously, and the server-selection specification permits a maximum-staleness eligibility filter. Query-placement isolation and acceptable replication lag require separate decisions. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-preference.md · keywords: Workload isolation with tagged secondaries and Atlas analytics nodes · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md
